title: Comment Spam Flood
description: Stop comment spam floods, clean thousands of spam comments, and prevent recurrence without breaking legitimate discussion.

steps.title: Assess Spam Volume and Source
steps.instructions: Check Comments admin for pending spam count. Note if spam targets one post or is site-wide. Check if comments are even needed on the site.

steps.title: Bulk Delete Existing Spam
steps.instructions: Use Comments → Spam → Empty Spam. For huge volumes, use WP-CLI: wp comment delete $(wp comment list --status=spam --format=ids) --force. Backup database first.

steps.title: Disable Comments Where Not Needed
steps.instructions: Turn off comments on pages and old posts via Settings → Discussion or bulk edit. Use a disable-comments plugin for site-wide shutdown if comments are unused.

steps.title: Enable Akismet or Anti-Spam Plugin
steps.instructions: Install Akismet, Antispam Bee, or CleanTalk. Configure API keys and test with a legitimate comment to ensure real comments are not blocked.

steps.title: Add Honeypot or CAPTCHA
steps.instructions: Add reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, or honeypot fields to comment forms. Balance friction — too aggressive blocks real users.

steps.title: Auto-Close Comments on Old Posts
steps.instructions: Enable 'Automatically close comments on posts older than X days' under Settings → Discussion. Most spam targets old high-traffic posts.

steps.title: Block Comment Spam Bots at Server Level
steps.instructions: Rate-limit comment POST requests in WAF or security plugin. Block known spam IP ranges and disable pingbacks if not needed.

steps.title: Monitor Comment Queue for 48 Hours
steps.instructions: Watch for new spam influx. Confirm legitimate comments still work if comments remain enabled. Document anti-spam stack for client.
